Strict mode: approximate and unsupported features fail loud

Source: R/registry.R
sasonr_strict.Rd

Every function, format and informat that sasonr implements has a status in the feature registry (sas_feature_registry()). The option sasonr.strict decides what happens when a program uses a feature that is not supported:

Details

  • TRUE (the default): the program stops with a condition of class sasonr_strict_error (a subclass of sasonr_unsupported) that names the SAS feature, its status and the SAS line. This applies to approximate features (the last bits of numeric results may not be exact), unsupported ones, features missing from the registry, and functions called in a context (DATA step, WHERE, PROC SQL, %SYSFUNC) in which they are not supported.

  • FALSE: the program runs with the R implementation's values. In sas_run() the log gets one NOTE at the end of the submission that lists the approximate features used (event id sasonr.approximate in $log_events, also when the submission stops with an error), and each feature signals one warning of class sasonr_strict_warning per submission. A direct call of a function-layer function (sas_f_*()) warns with class sasonr_strict_warning once per function and R session.

supported features, partial ones and clock-dependent not_comparable functions (TODAY(), DATE(), TIME(), DATETIME()) run in the contexts in which they are supported. Arguments outside the domain in which a function's results are exact (for example very large arguments of some date functions) are gated in the same way. Features that are not implemented at all fail loud with sasonr_unsupported in both modes.

The same rules apply when a function of the function layer (sas_f_*()) is called directly from R code: the function is checked as in a DATA step, sas_f_put() and sas_f_input() check their format or informat (given as text such as "8.2"), and arguments outside the exact input domain go through the strict gate. Where the DATA step writes a data-error NOTE or set _ERROR_ (an invalid argument, invalid data), a direct call returns the result a DATA step gives and signals a warning of class sasonr_data_error that carries the NOTE text.

Examples

# PROBT() is approximate: the last bits of some results may not be exact
try(sas_run("data a; y = probt(1.5, 10); run;"))
#> Error in strict_gate(what, line, feature = feature, fields = list(kind = kind,  : 
#>   function PROBT is approximate; set options(sasonr.strict = FALSE) to use it (SAS line 1)
res <- rlang::with_options(sasonr.strict = FALSE,
  suppressWarnings(sas_run("data a; y = probt(1.5, 10); run;")))
res$work$a$y
#> [1] 0.9177463
# the NOTE at the end of the log lists the approximate features
tail(res$log, 1)
#> [1] "NOTE: sasonr used approximate implementations: function PROBT."
